reason: The reviewed recovery implementation is substantially credible, but the unchanged broad world-class claim remains unproven. I traced the actual People account forms through new/existing identity linking, membership acknowledgement, restricted incident recording, queue inspection and resolution. The former missing-grant-receipt objection is addressed: route.ts:133–140 and 170–174 reject absent/nonstring membership IDs; account-provisioning.tsx:22–35 retains form details on unknown or malformed acknowledgements and resets only after a nonempty receipt. Recovery links preserve cycle context and explain that successful writes may have no incident. The queue's Back to People link preserves its cycle; the shared server selector honors URL-derived context and rechecks authorization. People tabs now implement associated panels, roving focus and arrow/Home/End navigation while keeping forms mounted. These are source and synthetic-test conclusions, not observed owner success. The SQL incident contract restricts identifying lookup data to current same-cycle owners; resolution changes neither accounts nor access and audits only an incident reference. Mocked route assertions and supplied 31-test/40-browser-check logs support the sampled failure paths. Public desktop/mobile captures show a coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy, readable proposition and restrained actions. Home states no fee and one semester, while partnerships remain explicitly distinct from approved work. The student journey source explains preparation, evaluation and unavailable dates; materials, final review and applicant receipt consistently disclose identifying original-resume access. These strengths do not establish hosted provisioning recovery, actual user understanding, complete accessible journeys or consulting proof. Consequently I cannot give unqualified agreement or certify deployment readiness from this package.
